entries.title: Narrator: "Symon Holl, Gus Manger and Lileas G..."
entries.dialogueText: Symon Holl, Gus Manger and Lileas Graf were about to arrive at the White Room for our scheduled economy meeting. This was the room in the Maroon Palace where all important meetings were held.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“My staff and I have comprehensivel..."

entries.title: Narrator: "He was interrupted by a groan from..."
entries.dialogueText: He was interrupted by a groan from one of the assistants by the door, both of whom were now visibly struggling to hold up the heavy projector.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He pointed below the painting of Pr..."
entries.dialogueText: He pointed below the painting of President Soll. The assistants placed the projector next to the table and installed a white screen on the wall.

entries.menuText: “What is our unemployment and inflation rate?”

entries.dialogueText: “Since economics is your forte, Mr. Rayne, it is possible that you might already be aware of the data. I can still explain the current economic situation in better detail.”

entries.menuText: Stay silent.

entries.dialogueText: “I am very well and motivated, Mr. Rayne. It seems our ministers are feeling the same.”

entries.dialogueText: “What is the status of the recession?”

entries.dialogueText: “Our current GDP is 310 billion Sordish Ren and the national debt is 427 billion.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“The economy has been in a recessio..."
entries.dialogueText: “The economy has been in a recession of about -6% in the past year. The average GDP has dropped from SR 15,454 per capita to SR 10,359 from 1951 to now.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Unemployment has skyrocketed and i..."
entries.dialogueText: “Unemployment has skyrocketed and is now at a staggering 16% and the inflation is at a relative high of 10%.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Symon scattered the paper stack in..."
entries.dialogueText: Symon scattered the paper stack in front of him in an orderly manner and took a final look at his notes before clearing his throat.

entries.dialogueText: "Don't be an idiot, Lileas. What about the unemployment crisis the Greater Holsord and Gelsland regions are going through? These areas are our economic heartland.”

entries.title: Symon Holl: "“The structural problems of Sollono..."
entries.dialogueText: “The structural problems of Sollonomics were going to lead to a recession according to the predictions at the time anyway. Either way, even if we pick one of the doctrines, we retain the option to make economic choices on a case-by-case basis.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“It is clear that most of the state..."
entries.dialogueText: “It is clear that most of the state corporations and other government controlled systems are less efficient.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Picking a construction company, tr..."
entries.dialogueText: “Picking a construction company, trade relations, tax reform and welfare privatization or nationalization initiatives would be some of them.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Sticking to a solid planned econom..."
entries.dialogueText: “Sticking to a solid planned economy strategy will be the right call. The five-year plans were fruitful in the past.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“It is important to think about thi..."
entries.dialogueText: “It is important to think about this subject because the upswings of the world economy will reflect good on ours too.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“That is, however, not recommended..."
entries.dialogueText: “That is, however, not recommended in my point of view. The last thing we need is a chaotic economic plan.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“The government of Sordland and its..."
entries.dialogueText: “The government of Sordland and its institutions or corporations have a solid history of delivering.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“We must choose wisely and remember..."
entries.dialogueText: “We must choose wisely and remember that the free-market economy in all forms is the future of the world.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Symon put forward a legal document..."
entries.dialogueText: Symon put forward a legal document outlining the possibilities with both economic doctrines listed. The cabinet members looked at me.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“What are your final thoughts, Mr...."
entries.dialogueText: “What are your final thoughts, Mr. President?”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Self-sufficiency will help us in t..."
entries.dialogueText: “Self-sufficiency will help us in tough times.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“Because the lack of competition ha..."
entries.dialogueText: “Because the lack of competition has made them inefficient.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Critical institutions must remain..."
entries.dialogueText: “Critical institutions must remain in state control. We must be fully responsible in delivering services.”
entries.menuText: “Critical institutions must remain in state control. We must be fully responsible in delivering services.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We should look at opportunities li..."
entries.dialogueText: “We should look at opportunities like privatization to create financial resources.”
entries.menuText: “We should look at opportunities like privatization to create financial resources.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“It is hard to fully agree or disag..."
entries.dialogueText: “It is hard to fully agree or disagree with these options.”
entries.menuText: “It is hard to fully agree or disagree with these options.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“A market economy doesn't mean priv..."
entries.dialogueText: “A market economy doesn't mean privatization of every single institution. But either way, you make the choices.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“This is exactly my mentality. Ther..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is exactly my mentality. There are many possibilities that are waiting, like education or health privatization. It would be better to promote a market economy for these to have consistency with our plan.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“It's a difficult position to be in..."
entries.dialogueText: “It's a difficult position to be in, Mr. President. But your final say is what counts. Remember, this is the overall strategic direction. Our ability to make individual economic decisions still remains.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Now that the economic direction was..."
entries.dialogueText: Now that the economic direction was decided upon, the ministers dispersed for lunch at the Maroon Palace.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Two assistants arrived first, carry..."
entries.dialogueText: Two assistants arrived first, carrying a heavy projector. They stood with it by the door, waiting for the ministers to enter.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“We will get there, Gus. No rush.”"
entries.dialogueText: “We will get there, Gus. No rush.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“Especially about lifting people ou..."
entries.dialogueText: “Especially about lifting people out of poverty. Certainly, a challenge.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“I am feeling fairly confident abou..."
entries.dialogueText: “I am feeling fairly confident about the current state of affairs.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Symon interrupted."
entries.dialogueText: Symon interrupted.

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Mr. Manger proposes that we should..."
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. Manger proposes that we should invest in already developed regions.”

entries.dialogueText: “We should support the city of Arvory and its respected mayor.”

entries.title: Gus Manger: "“That is simply untrue.”"
entries.dialogueText: “That is simply untrue.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“In return for what? Sordland's ind..."
entries.dialogueText: “In return for what? Sordland's independence?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Time will show if staying neutral..."
entries.dialogueText: “Time will show if staying neutral will work out.”
entries.menuText: “Time will show if staying neutral will work out.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Sordland will not be controlled by..."
entries.dialogueText: “Sordland will not be controlled by any nations.”
entries.menuText: “Sordland will not be controlled by any nations.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Exactly. Soll was right all along..."
entries.dialogueText: “Exactly. Soll was right all along with his policies.”
entries.menuText: “Exactly. Soll was right all along with his policies.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“I am glad we are on the same page...."
entries.dialogueText: “I am glad we are on the same page.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“I hope we won't regret this.”"
entries.dialogueText: “I hope we won't regret this.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Precisely my point. We will stand..."
entries.dialogueText: “Precisely my point. We will stand strong and show an example to the world.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I still haven't decided if they wi..."
entries.dialogueText: “I still haven't decided if they wish to come with a deal.”
entries.menuText: “I still haven't decided if they wish to come with a deal.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“A deal that they would surely come..."
entries.dialogueText: “A deal that they would surely come out with more profit while our people suffered.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“We don't know that. We should wait..."
entries.dialogueText: “We don't know that. We should wait and see. With the deals we could get by aligning ourselves with a strong country like Arcasia, recession would surely end in no time.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“We must make it work to protect ou..."
entries.dialogueText: “We must make it work to protect our country and our values. There is no other way.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“We need to be open to other possib..."
entries.dialogueText: “We need to be open to other possibilities. Arcasia is a strong country and If we end up in their sphere, Sordland would increase its influence in the world.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“The deals we would get would surel..."
entries.dialogueText: “The deals we would get would surely bring us out of recession.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“In return for what? Our independen..."
entries.dialogueText: “In return for what? Our independence?”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Economically speaking, we are much..."
entries.dialogueText: “Economically speaking, we are much closer to Arcasia than United Contana, so a decision to align with the west makes more sense.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Economically speaking, we aren't a..."
entries.dialogueText: “Economically speaking, we aren't as tied to United Contana as we are to Arcasia, so a decision to align with the east is much more difficult to accomplish.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Economically speaking, an isolatio..."
entries.dialogueText: “Economically speaking, an isolationist policy overall could only work if we were to reap the benefits of both spheres and their rivalry. This is very dangerous to attempt but still possible.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The more of the economy we control..."
entries.dialogueText: “The more of the economy we control, the better we can manage the recession.”
entries.menuText: “The more of the economy we control, the better we can manage the recession.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Economic systems without regulatio..."
entries.dialogueText: “Economic systems without regulation are bound to fail.”
entries.menuText: “Economic systems without regulation are bound to fail.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Humanity in the 20th century is th..."
entries.dialogueText: “Humanity in the 20th century is thriving because of the rule of supply and demand.”
entries.menuText: “Humanity in the 20th century is thriving because of the rule of supply and demand.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“From taxes to the standard of good..."
entries.dialogueText: “From taxes to the standard of goods, there are many elements that regulate all aspects of this system.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“But is it enough? I doubt it. If w..."
entries.dialogueText: “But is it enough? I doubt it. If we can manage to plan more aspects of the economy, our chances of success would increase with a talented team like ours.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Obviously there is some regulation..."
entries.dialogueText: “Obviously there is some regulation in all of the existing systems, otherwise it would be anarchy. Nobody wants a chaotic society.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“One way to be remembered positivel..."
entries.dialogueText: “One way to be remembered positively is to cause a recession and leave a few bills behind.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“Say what you will about Alphonso,..."
entries.dialogueText: “Say what you will about Alphonso, without his attempts our current coffers would be empty and the recession would be a depression.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“That is a fair argument to be made..."
entries.dialogueText: “That is a fair argument to be made. But if we reduce the freedom of people in the market place in general, it would hinder our innovation and dynamism in the supply and demand equation.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Integrating heavily in a market ec..."
entries.dialogueText: “Integrating heavily in a market economy would work if we had extensive means of production. Our industry is lacking.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“Sordland has the potential to do s..."
entries.dialogueText: “Sordland has the potential to do so as well. Why don't we take our potential seriously?”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Agreed. Look at how quickly Lespia..."
entries.dialogueText: “Agreed. Look at how quickly Lespia and Arcasia have increased their prosperity by embracing these basic principles.”

entries.dialogueText: “The primary subject we need to settle on is what general path we will take in our term. Sollonomics-based nationalization happened in the '30s and Alphonso's privatization began during the end of the '40s. What will our administration focus on?”
